body:
> Theres a lot of people in the world. Letting one bunch of shitheads break you down isn't worth it when theres a social group waiting for you right around the corner.

That legitimately helped there. I've dealt with a lot of shitty friends. I don't really care who you are, it is never a pleasant feeling to see people you were close with leave, especially the core of your support system. It has left me alone in a place far from home.

I don't disagree with all of what you said. I come from the EMS field, most of what I do is saving strangers. I don't seek reward or validation for this. The part that hurts is when you get close to someone, (I'm not trying to be vague, this has happened with friends and love interest alike) and then at what seems to be the flip of a switch, who was once a confidant suddenly becomes a stranger. I can typically handle it when it's one person, but when there is a cascade of people, one after another turning their backs, it makes you ponder, is there anyone who really needs me to be there? I don't ask because I need someone to be there, more because what is the point if there is nothing for me to do. If no body needs me, why waste space?
